- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T12:10:44Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1391

## Root cause (drilled, not guessed)

All four drillable PTY-family reds in the #1391 window show the SAME signature — one test popping a quiet-runner wait budget inside an otherwise-green 60–70-test shard:

| run / job | failing test | signature |
|---|---|---|
| 114115713413 (PTY shard 0/3) | header_badge_pty (#1469) | `TimeoutException after 30s` waiting the fold badge while a double-compaction turn was still painting |
| 114064133950 (PTY shard 2/3) | fa_tui_follow_pty (#1467) | `expect(contains 'above fold')` read a frame from a LATER state — raced mid-run capture |
| 113385178088 (PTY shard 0/3) | pty_resume_equivalence (#1422) | live transcript captured one probe behind the resumed one — capture raced the turn |
| 114167806111 (PTY shard 0/3) | header_badge_pty (#1469) | same 30s budget pop on a different head |

Mechanism: SM dispatch waves run 2+ full CI runs concurrently on the hosted ubuntu-24.04-arm pool (refresh waves supersede PR heads mid-run); every CLI spawn, mock-LLM round trip, compaction pass and TUI repaint stretches, and fixed wall-clock budgets (harness defaults 10–90s, per-test up to 60s) pop. Window-intermittent, dispatch-correlated — matches the fleet tally in the issue (9 green re-roll heads vs 2 red dispatch windows; canary green).

## Delivered

- `lib/src/cli/pty_wait_budget.dart` — flutter-free, env-injected scale resolver (`FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE`): blank/garbage fail open to 1.0 (a workflow typo can never red a leg); clamps to [1.0, 10.0] — the scale never SHRINKS a budget and never turns a real hang into an unbounded wait.
- `FaCliHarness` + `CliVisualHarness` — every wait budget (`waitForBoot/Text/Screen/Raw/Output`, settle, raw-settle grace) multiplied by the ambient scale. Unset → 1.0 → byte-identical legacy behavior locally and in the nightly (nightly stays unsupervised flake evidence for quarantine decisions).
- `ci.yml` — `FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE: '2'` on exactly the two legs the issue names: `PTY/CLI integration (linux, shard N/3)` and `Terminal visual (PTY screenshots, PR)`.
- Regression tests: `test/cli/pty_wait_budget_test.dart` (10 unit tests, no PTY needed — parse semantics, clamping, multiplication, overflow safety).

## Scope discipline

- Sibling lanes (#1385 #1413 #1422 #1467 #1469) keep ownership of their tests' content fixes — this changes zero test files' logic, only the shared wait ceilings the dispatch waves blow through.
- Quarantined files untouched; no `scripts/test_quarantine.json` churn.
- Nightly + integration-mock legs deliberately left unscaled.
- The per-test duration budget gate (#928) is unaffected: green-run durations don't change (match-exits stay early; only give-up deadlines stretch), and the gate never sees red-run durations (`needs: [pty-integration-linux]`).

## Local gates

- `dart analyze` on all changed Dart files: zero issues (full-repo analyze: 132 pre-existing infos identical with/without the diff — analyzer-version skew, none in changed files).
- `dart format`: clean.
- `dart test test/cli/pty_wait_budget_test.dart test/ci_pty_artifact_upload_retry_guard_test.dart`: 14/14 green (incl. the YAML-shape guard over the edited ci.yml).
- flutter_app: `flutter analyze test/cli_visual/cli_visual_harness.dart` clean; `flutter test test/cli_visual/cli_visual_harness_env_test.dart` 14/14 green (verified on a local Flutter 3.47.5 copy).
- Live PTY execution is impossible in this sandbox (`openpty` denied, `/tmp` read-only) — the four drilled CI runs above are the reproduction evidence; the change is exercised by the merge-blocking legs themselves on the next SM validation.

## Remaining

- None in this lane. Un-quarantine decisions for the five sibling tests ride their own issues; if their budgets (not their content) were the binding constraint, this seam already covers them via the same harness paths.

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review…

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1488
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1488
- **Title**: fix(1391): load-aware PTY wait budgets — FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE on the two merge-blocking PTY legs
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1391-pty-visual-flake` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 5
- **Additions**: +208
- **Deletions**: -8
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T12:10:44Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T12:10:44Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1391

## Root cause (drilled, not guessed)

All four drillable PTY-family reds in the #1391 window show the SAME signature — one test popping a quiet-runner wait budget inside an otherwise-green 60–70-test shard:

| run / job | failing test | signature |
|---|---|---|
| 114115713413 (PTY shard 0/3) | header_badge_pty (#1469) | `TimeoutException after 30s` waiting the fold badge while a double-compaction turn was still painting |
| 114064133950 (PTY shard 2/3) | fa_tui_follow_pty (#1467) | `expect(contains 'above fold')` read a frame from a LATER state — raced mid-run capture |
| 113385178088 (PTY shard 0/3) | pty_resume_equivalence (#1422) | live transcript captured one probe behind the resumed one — capture raced the turn |
| 114167806111 (PTY shard 0/3) | header_badge_pty (#1469) | same 30s budget pop on a different head |

Mechanism: SM dispatch waves run 2+ full CI runs concurrently on the hosted ubuntu-24.04-arm pool (refresh waves supersede PR heads mid-run); every CLI spawn, mock-LLM round trip, compaction pass and TUI repaint stretches, and fixed wall-clock budgets (harness defaults 10–90s, per-test up to 60s) pop. Window-intermittent, dispatch-correlated — matches the fleet tally in the issue (9 green re-roll heads vs 2 red dispatch windows; canary green).

## Delivered

- `lib/src/cli/pty_wait_budget.dart` — flutter-free, env-injected scale resolver (`FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE`): blank/garbage fail open to 1.0 (a workflow typo can never red a leg); clamps to [1.0, 10.0] — the scale never SHRINKS a budget and never turns a real hang into an unbounded wait.
- `FaCliHarness` + `CliVisualHarness` — every wait budget (`waitForBoot/Text/Screen/Raw/Output`, settle, raw-settle grace) multiplied by the ambient scale. Unset → 1.0 → byte-identical legacy behavior locally and in the nightly (nightly stays unsupervised flake evidence for quarantine decisions).
- `ci.yml` — `FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE: '2'` on exactly the two legs the issue names: `PTY/CLI integration (linux, shard N/3)` and `Terminal visual (PTY screenshots, PR)`.
- Regression tests: `test/cli/pty_wait_budget_test.dart` (10 unit tests, no PTY needed — parse semantics, clamping, multiplication, overflow safety).

## Scope discipline

- Sibling lanes (#1385 #1413 #1422 #1467 #1469) keep ownership of their tests' content fixes — this changes zero test files' logic, only the shared wait ceilings the dispatch waves blow through.
- Quarantined files untouched; no `scripts/test_quarantine.json` churn.
- Nightly + integration-mock legs deliberately left unscaled.
- The per-test duration budget gate (#928) is unaffected: green-run durations don't change (match-exits stay early; only give-up deadlines stretch), and the gate never sees red-run durations (`needs: [pty-integration-linux]`).

## Local gates

- `dart analyze` on all changed Dart files: zero issues (full-repo analyze: 132 pre-existing infos identical with/without the diff — analyzer-version skew, none in changed files).
- `dart format`: clean.
- `dart test test/cli/pty_wait_budget_test.dart test/ci_pty_artifact_upload_retry_guard_test.dart`: 14/14 green (incl. the YAML-shape guard over the edited ci.yml).
- flutter_app: `flutter analyze test/cli_visual/cli_visual_harness.dart` clean; `flutter test test/cli_visual/cli_visual_harness_env_test.dart` 14/14 green (verified on a local Flutter 3.47.5 copy).
- Live PTY execution is impossible in this sandbox (`openpty` denied, `/tmp` read-only) — the four drilled CI runs above are the reproduction evidence; the change is exercised by the merge-blocking legs themselves on the next SM validation.

## Remaining

- None in this lane. Un-quarantine decisions for the five sibling tests ride their own issues; if their budgets (not their content) were the binding constraint, this seam already covers them via the same harness paths.

- run: dart pub get

      # before/after numbers.
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: fa-aot-bin
          path: fa-local/bundle
      # Artifact zips do NOT preserve the exec bit (download-artifact
      # README: "post-download the file is no longer guaranteed to be set
      # as an executable"). Run 37446280743: `test -x` below failed
      # silently ~20 ms in on EVERY shard — the gate went red before a
      # single test ran. Restore the mode the build job shipped; the
      # smoke below still verifies the restored binary is executable and
      # boots (never a silent JIT fallback). Content integrity is not
      # affected: download-artifact digest-validates (digest-mismatch:
      # error default), so this chmod only ever touches the verified
      # bundle the fa-aot-build job produced.
      - name: Restore exec bit (artifact zips drop permissions)
        run: chmod +x fa-local/bundle/bin/fah
      - name: Smoke the AOT binary (fail loud, never JIT-fallback)

          test -x fa-local/bundle/bin/fah
          ./fa-local/bundle/bin/fah --version

- **PR #**: 1488
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1488
- **Title**: fix(1391): load-aware PTY wait budgets — FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE on the two merge-blocking PTY legs
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1391-pty-visual-flake` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 5
- **Additions**: +208
- **Deletions**: -8
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T12:10:44Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T12:10:44Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1391

## Root cause (drilled, not guessed)

All four drillable PTY-family reds in the #1391 window show the SAME signature — one test popping a quiet-runner wait budget inside an otherwise-green 60–70-test shard:

| run / job | failing test | signature |
|---|---|---|
| 114115713413 (PTY shard 0/3) | header_badge_pty (#1469) | `TimeoutException after 30s` waiting the fold badge while a double-compaction turn was still painting |
| 114064133950 (PTY shard 2/3) | fa_tui_follow_pty (#1467) | `expect(contains 'above fold')` read a frame from a LATER state — raced mid-run capture |
| 113385178088 (PTY shard 0/3) | pty_resume_equivalence (#1422) | live transcript captured one probe behind the resumed one — capture raced the turn |
| 114167806111 (PTY shard 0/3) | header_badge_pty (#1469) | same 30s budget pop on a different head |

Mechanism: SM dispatch waves run 2+ full CI runs concurrently on the hosted ubuntu-24.04-arm pool (refresh waves supersede PR heads mid-run); every CLI spawn, mock-LLM round trip, compaction pass and TUI repaint stretches, and fixed wall-clock budgets (harness defaults 10–90s, per-test up to 60s) pop. Window-intermittent, dispatch-correlated — matches the fleet tally in the issue (9 green re-roll heads vs 2 red dispatch windows; canary green).

## Delivered

- `lib/src/cli/pty_wait_budget.dart` — flutter-free, env-injected scale resolver (`FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE`): blank/garbage fail open to 1.0 (a workflow typo can never red a leg); clamps to [1.0, 10.0] — the scale never SHRINKS a budget and never turns a real hang into an unbounded wait.
- `FaCliHarness` + `CliVisualHarness` — every wait budget (`waitForBoot/Text/Screen/Raw/Output`, settle, raw-settle grace) multiplied by the ambient scale. Unset → 1.0 → byte-identical legacy behavior locally and in the nightly (nightly stays unsupervised flake evidence for quarantine decisions).
- `ci.yml` — `FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE: '2'` on exactly the two legs the issue names: `PTY/CLI integration (linux, shard N/3)` and `Terminal visual (PTY screenshots, PR)`.
- Regression tests: `test/cli/pty_wait_budget_test.dart` (10 unit tests, no PTY needed — parse semantics, clamping, multiplication, overflow safety).

## Scope discipline

- Sibling lanes (#1385 #1413 #1422 #1467 #1469) keep ownership of their tests' content fixes — this changes zero test files' logic, only the shared wait ceilings the dispatch waves blow through.
- Quarantined files untouched; no `scripts/test_quarantine.json` churn.
- Nightly + integration-mock legs deliberately left unscaled.
- The per-test duration budget gate (#928) is unaffected: green-run durations don't change (match-exits stay early; only give-up deadlines stretch), and the gate never sees red-run durations (`needs: [pty-integration-linux]`).

## Local gates

- `dart analyze` on all changed Dart files: zero issues (full-repo analyze: 132 pre-existing infos identical with/without the diff — analyzer-version skew, none in changed files).
- `dart format`: clean.
- `dart test test/cli/pty_wait_budget_test.dart test/ci_pty_artifact_upload_retry_guard_test.dart`: 14/14 green (incl. the YAML-shape guard over the edited ci.yml).
- flutter_app: `flutter analyze test/cli_visual/cli_visual_harness.dart` clean; `flutter test test/cli_visual/cli_visual_harness_env_test.dart` 14/14 green (verified on a local Flutter 3.47.5 copy).
- Live PTY execution is impossible in this sandbox (`openpty` denied, `/tmp` read-only) — the four drilled CI runs above are the reproduction evidence; the change is exercised by the merge-blocking legs themselves on the next SM validation.

## Remaining

- None in this lane. Un-quarantine decisions for the five sibling tests ride their own issues; if their budgets (not their content) were the binding constraint, this seam already covers them via the same harness paths.

- run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache

          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      # guard FAILS the shard loudly if the artifact is missing or dead —
      # a silent JIT fallback would hide the optimization from AC1's
      # before/after numbers.
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: fa-aot-bin
          path: fa-local/bundle
      # Artifact zips do NOT preserve the exec bit (download-artifact
      # README: "post-download the file is no longer guaranteed to be set
      # as an executable"). Run 37446280743: `test -x` below failed
      # silently ~20 ms in on EVERY shard — the gate went red before a
      # single test ran. Restore the mode the build job shipped; the
      # smoke below still verifies the restored binary is executable and
      # boots (never a silent JIT fallback). Content integrity is not
      # affected: download-artifact digest-validates (digest-mismatch:
      # error default), so this chmod only ever touches the verified
      # bundle the fa-aot-build job produced.
      - name: Restore exec bit (artifact zips drop permissions)
        run: chmod +x fa-local/bundle/bin/fah
      - name: Smoke the AOT binary (fail loud, never JIT-fallback)
        run: |
          test -x fa-local/bundle/bin/fah
          ./fa-local/bundle/bin/fah --version
      - name: dart test --tags integration (linux, shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/3)

    # gh-1300: needs the once-per-run AOT build; FA_BIN points every CLI

- **Title**: fix(1391): load-aware PTY wait budgets — FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE on the two merge-blocking PTY legs
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1391-pty-visual-flake` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 5

- **Created**: 2026-10-10T12:10:44Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T12:10:44Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1391

## Root cause (drilled, not guessed)

All four drillable PTY-family reds in the #1391 window show the SAME signature — one test popping a quiet-runner wait budget inside an otherwise-green 60–70-test shard:

| run / job | failing test | signature |
|---|---|---|
| 114115713413 (PTY shard 0/3) | header_badge_pty (#1469) | `TimeoutException after 30s` waiting the fold badge while a double-compaction turn was still painting |
| 114064133950 (PTY shard 2/3) | fa_tui_follow_pty (#1467) | `expect(contains 'above fold')` read a frame from a LATER state — raced mid-run capture |
| 113385178088 (PTY shard 0/3) | pty_resume_equivalence (#1422) | live transcript captured one probe behind the resumed one — capture raced the turn |
| 114167806111 (PTY shard 0/3) | header_badge_pty (#1469) | same 30s budget pop on a different head |

Mechanism: SM dispatch waves run 2+ full CI runs concurrently on the hosted ubuntu-24.04-arm pool (refresh waves supersede PR heads mid-run); every CLI spawn, mock-LLM round trip, compaction pass and TUI repaint stretches, and fixed wall-clock budgets (harness defaults 10–90s, per-test up to 60s) pop. Window-intermittent, dispatch-correlated — matches the fleet tally in the issue (9 green re-roll heads vs 2 red dispatch windows; canary green).

## Delivered

- `lib/src/cli/pty_wait_budget.dart` — flutter-free, env-injected scale resolver (`FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE`): blank/garbage fail open to 1.0 (a workflow typo can never red a leg); clamps to [1.0, 10.0] — the scale never SHRINKS a budget and never turns a real hang into an unbounded wait.
- `FaCliHarness` + `CliVisualHarness` — every wait budget (`waitForBoot/Text/Screen/Raw/Output`, settle, raw-settle grace) multiplied by the ambient scale. Unset → 1.0 → byte-identical legacy behavior locally and in the nightly (nightly stays unsupervised flake evidence for quarantine decisions).
- `ci.yml` — `FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE: '2'` on exactly the two legs the issue names: `PTY/CLI integration (linux, shard N/3)` and `Terminal visual (PTY screenshots, PR)`.
- Regression tests: `test/cli/pty_wait_budget_test.dart` (10 unit tests, no PTY needed — parse semantics, clamping, multiplication, overflow safety).

## Scope discipline

- Sibling lanes (#1385 #1413 #1422 #1467 #1469) keep ownership of their tests' content fixes — this changes zero test files' logic, only the shared wait ceilings the dispatch waves blow through.
- Quarantined files untouched; no `scripts/test_quarantine.json` churn.
- Nightly + integration-mock legs deliberately left unscaled.
- The per-test duration budget gate (#928) is unaffected: green-run durations don't change (match-exits stay early; only give-up deadlines stretch), and the gate never sees red-run durations (`needs: [pty-integration-linux]`).

## Local gates

- `dart analyze` on all changed Dart files: zero issues (full-repo analyze: 132 pre-existing infos identical with/without the diff — analyzer-version skew, none in changed files).
- `dart format`: clean.
- `dart test test/cli/pty_wait_budget_test.dart test/ci_pty_artifact_upload_retry_guard_test.dart`: 14/14 green (incl. the YAML-shape guard over the edited ci.yml).
- flutter_app: `flutter analyze test/cli_visual/cli_visual_harness.dart` clean; `flutter test test/cli_visual/cli_visual_harness_env_test.dart` 14/14 green (verified on a local Flutter 3.47.5 copy).
- Live PTY execution is impossible in this sandbox (`openpty` denied, `/tmp` read-only) — the four drilled CI runs above are the reproduction evidence; the change is exercised by the merge-blocking legs themselves on the next SM validation.

## Remaining

- None in this lane. Un-quarantine decisions for the five sibling tests ride their own issues; if their budgets (not their content) were the binding constraint, this seam already covers them via the same harness paths.

      - name: Restore exec bit (artifact zips drop permissions)

- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T12:10:44Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1391

## Root cause (drilled, not guessed)

All four drillable PTY-family reds in the #1391 window show the SAME signature — one test popping a quiet-runner wait budget inside an otherwise-green 60–70-test shard:

| run / job | failing test | signature |
|---|---|---|
| 114115713413 (PTY shard 0/3) | header_badge_pty (#1469) | `TimeoutException after 30s` waiting the fold badge while a double-compaction turn was still painting |
| 114064133950 (PTY shard 2/3) | fa_tui_follow_pty (#1467) | `expect(contains 'above fold')` read a frame from a LATER state — raced mid-run capture |
| 113385178088 (PTY shard 0/3) | pty_resume_equivalence (#1422) | live transcript captured one probe behind the resumed one — capture raced the turn |
| 114167806111 (PTY shard 0/3) | header_badge_pty (#1469) | same 30s budget pop on a different head |

Mechanism: SM dispatch waves run 2+ full CI runs concurrently on the hosted ubuntu-24.04-arm pool (refresh waves supersede PR heads mid-run); every CLI spawn, mock-LLM round trip, compaction pass and TUI repaint stretches, and fixed wall-clock budgets (harness defaults 10–90s, per-test up to 60s) pop. Window-intermittent, dispatch-correlated — matches the fleet tally in the issue (9 green re-roll heads vs 2 red dispatch windows; canary green).

## Delivered

- `lib/src/cli/pty_wait_budget.dart` — flutter-free, env-injected scale resolver (`FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE`): blank/garbage fail open to 1.0 (a workflow typo can never red a leg); clamps to [1.0, 10.0] — the scale never SHRINKS a budget and never turns a real hang into an unbounded wait.
- `FaCliHarness` + `CliVisualHarness` — every wait budget (`waitForBoot/Text/Screen/Raw/Output`, settle, raw-settle grace) multiplied by the ambient scale. Unset → 1.0 → byte-identical legacy behavior locally and in the nightly (nightly stays unsupervised flake evidence for quarantine decisions).
- `ci.yml` — `FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE: '2'` on exactly the two legs the issue names: `PTY/CLI integration (linux, shard N/3)` and `Terminal visual (PTY screenshots, PR)`.
- Regression tests: `test/cli/pty_wait_budget_test.dart` (10 unit tests, no PTY needed — parse semantics, clamping, multiplication, overflow safety).

## Scope discipline

- Sibling lanes (#1385 #1413 #1422 #1467 #1469) keep ownership of their tests' content fixes — this changes zero test files' logic, only the shared wait ceilings the dispatch waves blow through.
- Quarantined files untouched; no `scripts/test_quarantine.json` churn.
- Nightly + integration-mock legs deliberately left unscaled.
- The per-test duration budget gate (#928) is unaffected: green-run durations don't change (match-exits stay early; only give-up deadlines stretch), and the gate never sees red-run durations (`needs: [pty-integration-linux]`).

## Local gates

- `dart analyze` on all changed Dart files: zero issues (full-repo analyze: 132 pre-existing infos identical with/without the diff — analyzer-version skew, none in changed files).
- `dart format`: clean.
- `dart test test/cli/pty_wait_budget_test.dart test/ci_pty_artifact_upload_retry_guard_test.dart`: 14/14 green (incl. the YAML-shape guard over the edited ci.yml).
- flutter_app: `flutter analyze test/cli_visual/cli_visual_harness.dart` clean; `flutter test test/cli_visual/cli_visual_harness_env_test.dart` 14/14 green (verified on a local Flutter 3.47.5 copy).
- Live PTY execution is impossible in this sandbox (`openpty` denied, `/tmp` read-only) — the four drilled CI runs above are the reproduction evidence; the change is exercised by the merge-blocking legs themselves on the next SM validation.

## Remaining

- None in this lane. Un-quarantine decisions for the five sibling tests ride their own issues; if their budgets (not their content) were the binding constraint, this seam already covers them via the same harness paths.

          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      # guard FAILS the shard loudly if the artifact is missing or dead —
      # a silent JIT fallback would hide the optimization from AC1's
      # before/after numbers.
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: fa-aot-bin
          path: fa-local/bundle
      # Artifact zips do NOT preserve the exec bit (download-artifact
      # README: "post-download the file is no longer guaranteed to be set
      # as an executable"). Run 37446280743: `test -x` below failed
      # silently ~20 ms in on EVERY shard — the gate went red before a
      # single test ran. Restore the mode the build job shipped; the
      # smoke below still verifies the restored binary is executable and
      # boots (never a silent JIT fallback). Content integrity is not
      # affected: download-artifact digest-validates (digest-mismatch:
      # error default), so this chmod only ever touches the verified
      # bundle the fa-aot-build job produced.
      - name: Restore exec bit (artifact zips drop permissions)
        run: chmod +x fa-local/bundle/bin/fah
      - name: Smoke the AOT binary (fail loud, never JIT-fallback)

          test -x fa-local/bundle/bin/fah
          ./fa-local/bundle/bin/fah --version

pty-integration-linux:
    # THE PR PTY/CLI integration leg (gh-1005: the former mac leg merged in;
    # before that, issue #931 part 2 sharded ONE ~40-min job into 3
    # duration-balanced shards — scripts/test_integration_shards.json,
    # file-level units). New integration-tagged files bin-pack in at runtime
    # (shard_files.py --tags integration), so a PR adding one never
    # silently skips it. Explicit --concurrency=4 bounds in-suite
    # parallelism (part 3.3 — package:test forbids `concurrency` in
    # dart_test.yaml tag overrides, so the knob lives here; it bounds
    # concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB — the rate-limit rationale is
    # documented on the llm tag in dart_test.yaml).
    # Per-shard coverage artifacts merge in pty-coverage-gate —
    # a single shard's ratchet would see partial lib/src/cli coverage
    # and false-regress. Each shard also emits the dart json
    # file-reporter: junit feeds rebalancing/budget-tightening PRs, the
    # raw json feeds the #928 duration gate (pty-coverage-gate below).
    # gh-1300: needs the once-per-run AOT build; FA_BIN points every CLI
    # spawn (PTY harness + headless helpers) at the prebuilt binary.
    needs: [fa-aot-build]
    name: PTY/CLI integration (linux, shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/3)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    # 40 > 30: the leg now carries the coverage + file-reporter overhead the
    # old mac leg had (the coverage-free linux twin never paid it) and arm64
    # Graviton cores run somewhat slower than the M-series minis did — margin
    # without stretching the watchdog much.
    timeout-minutes: 40
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1, 2]
    env:
      # Secret shape (review 2026-09-23): this is the pull_request-time leg
      # that receives real provider secrets. GitHub withholds secrets from
      # forks, so external contributions never see them — but every
      # SAME-REPO branch runs this suite with the keys in its process
      # environment before human review (this repo's agent-authored-branch
      # model). The marginal escalation vs the nightly (same suites, same
      # keys, post-merge on main) is small and the watchdog already hands
      # RELEASE_PAT to same-repo PRs; documented here so the assumption is
      # explicit, not implicit.
      #
      # The live-provider legs (unlocked by these keys) load extra
      # lib/src/cli surface into the coverage measurement, so a no-key run
      # measures a DIFFERENT — lower-numbered — value; missing keys (forks)
      # self-skip those legs gracefully and the gate stays honest either
      # way.
      OPENROUTER_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENROUTER_API_KEY }}
      ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
      GOOGLE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GOOGLE_API_KEY }}
      OLLAMA_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OLLAMA_API_KEY }}

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,

callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review…

      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1

      - name: Restore exec bit (artifact zips drop permissions)

  # screen text (never pixels — each PNG even ships a .txt twin "for
  # pixel-independent verification"), rendering goes through the BUNDLED
  # JetBrainsMono font (no host system fonts), and pty2 allocates the PTY
  # via libc openpty FFI. Nothing needs macOS — the old fa-m5 / macos-latest
  # routing (10x hosted-macOS minute cost, single-runner queue risk) is
  # gone; the nightly keeps an eyeball-only screenshot leg.
  pty-visual:
    name: Terminal visual (PTY screenshots, PR)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: changes
    timeout-minutes: 45
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      # arm64: no official linux-arm64 release tarball (x64-only manifest) —
      # subosito/flutter-action cannot fetch stable here. Git bootstrap
      # (same as the flutter-tests leg): flutter_tools pulls the official
      # arm64 Dart SDK itself.
      - name: Flutter SDK (arm64 git bootstrap)
        shell: bash
        run: |
          git clone --depth 1 -b stable https://github.com/flutter/flutter.git "$HOME/flutter"
          echo "$HOME/flutter/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
          export PATH="$HOME/flutter/bin:$PATH"
          flutter --version
          flutter precache
      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('**/pubspec.yaml') }}
          restore-keys: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: touch .env
      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart
      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get
      # The harness spawns `dart bin/fah.dart` FROM THE REPO ROOT; without
      # a root package config it resolves the package to the pub-cache copy
      # (an old published build) and the CLI dies before the first frame.
      - run: dart pub get
      # Issue #943 (vector 3): warm the build hooks — the cli_visual harness
      # spawns `dart bin/fah.dart` from the repo root and its boot budget
      # must not pay the cold-hook cost (tui_prototype_snapshot ×5).
      - name: Prewarm build hooks + fa boot
        run: |
          dart bin/fah.dart --help > /dev/null
          dart run bin/fah.dart --help > /dev/null
      - name: flutter test test/cli_visual --tags integration
        env:
          # Issue #1391: same load-stretch as the PTY/CLI shards above —
          # this merge-blocking leg drives the real CLI through the same
          # harness waits and shares the dispatch-wave packing.
          FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE: '2'
        run: cd flutter_app && flutter test test/cli_visual --tags integration
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        if: always()
        with:
          name: cli-visual-screenshots-pr
          path: test/integration/screenshots/
          retention-days: 7

  coverage-gate:
    name: Coverage ratchet

Now, an important consideration: the pty-visual job has `timeout-minutes: 45`. Scaling waits 2x means a genuinely hung test would wait up to 2x the per-test budget (up to 60s → 120s). The job-level 45-min timeout still bounds it. OK.

Also check: the pty-integration-linux job timeout-minutes. And whether there's a job-level timeout that 2x budgets could exceed... unlikely.

Now the duration budget gate (#928): "the gate never sees red-run durations (needs: [pty-integration-linux])". Actually the gate runs `if: always()` probably on pty-integration-linux outputs. Green-run durations don't change because match-exits stay early. True — scaling only stretches the give-up deadline; a passing test that matched early exits early. But wait: does scaling affect settle-based waits that pass? E.g., `waitForRawSettle` — it waits until quiet for settleMs twice; scaling only extends grace deadline. Passing tests exit at same time. True.

One subtlety: `waitForOutput(settleMs, timeout)` in FaCliHarness at line ~470: loop `while (now < deadline)` with delayed settleMs between polls. If content matches early, exits early. OK.

Now check ci.yml job timeout for pty-integration-linux.

pty-integration-linux:
    # THE PR PTY/CLI integration leg (gh-1005: the former mac leg merged in;
    # before that, issue #931 part 2 sharded ONE ~40-min job into 3
    # duration-balanced shards — scripts/test_integration_shards.json,
    # file-level units). New integration-tagged files bin-pack in at runtime
    # (shard_files.py --tags integration), so a PR adding one never
    # silently skips it. Explicit --concurrency=4 bounds in-suite
    # parallelism (part 3.3 — package:test forbids `concurrency` in
    # dart_test.yaml tag overrides, so the knob lives here; it bounds
    # concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB — the rate-limit rationale is
    # documented on the llm tag in dart_test.yaml).
    # Per-shard coverage artifacts merge in pty-coverage-gate —
    # a single shard's ratchet would see partial lib/src/cli coverage
    # and false-regress. Each shard also emits the dart json
    # file-reporter: junit feeds rebalancing/budget-tightening PRs, the
    # raw json feeds the #928 duration gate (pty-coverage-gate below).
    # gh-1300: needs the once-per-run AOT build; FA_BIN points every CLI
    # spawn (PTY harness + headless helpers) at the prebuilt binary.
    needs: [fa-aot-build]
    name: PTY/CLI integration (linux, shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/3)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    # 40 > 30: the leg now carries the coverage + file-reporter overhead the
    # old mac leg had (the coverage-free linux twin never paid it) and arm64
    # Graviton cores run somewhat slower than the M-series minis did — margin
    # without stretching the watchdog much.
    timeout-minutes: 40
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1, 2]
    env:
      # Secret shape (review 2026-09-23): this is the pull_request-time leg
      # that receives real provider secrets. GitHub withholds secrets from
      # forks, so external contributions never see them — but every
      # SAME-REPO branch runs this suite with the keys in its process
      # environment before human review (this repo's agent-authored-branch
      # model). The marginal escalation vs the nightly (same suites, same
      # keys, post-merge on main) is small and the watchdog already hands
      # RELEASE_PAT to same-repo PRs; documented here so the assumption is
      # explicit, not implicit.
      #
      # The live-provider legs (unlocked by these keys) load extra
      # lib/src/cli surface into the coverage measurement, so a no-key run
      # measures a DIFFERENT — lower-numbered — value; missing keys (forks)
      # self-skip those legs gracefully and the gate stays honest either
      # way.
      OPENROUTER_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENROUTER_API_KEY }}
      ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
      GOOGLE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GOOGLE_API_KEY }}
      OLLAMA_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OLLAMA_API_KEY }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared

re-read changed files,

pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. - **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1391-pty-visual-flake` → `main`
- **State**: open

- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T12:10:44Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1391

## Root cause (drilled, not guessed)

All four drillable PTY-family reds in the #1391 window show the SAME signature — one test popping a quiet-runner wait budget inside an otherwise-green 60–70-test shard:

| run / job | failing test | signature |
|---|---|---|
| 114115713413 (PTY shard 0/3) | header_badge_pty (#1469) | `TimeoutException after 30s` waiting the fold badge while a double-compaction turn was still painting |
| 114064133950 (PTY shard 2/3) | fa_tui_follow_pty (#1467) | `expect(contains 'above fold')` read a frame from a LATER state — raced mid-run capture |
| 113385178088 (PTY shard 0/3) | pty_resume_equivalence (#1422) | live transcript captured one probe behind the resumed one — capture raced the turn |
| 114167806111 (PTY shard 0/3) | header_badge_pty (#1469) | same 30s budget pop on a different head |

Mechanism: SM dispatch waves run 2+ full CI runs concurrently on the hosted ubuntu-24.04-arm pool (refresh waves supersede PR heads mid-run); every CLI spawn, mock-LLM round trip, compaction pass and TUI repaint stretches, and fixed wall-clock budgets (harness defaults 10–90s, per-test up to 60s) pop. Window-intermittent, dispatch-correlated — matches the fleet tally in the issue (9 green re-roll heads vs 2 red dispatch windows; canary green).

## Delivered

- `lib/src/cli/pty_wait_budget.dart` — flutter-free, env-injected scale resolver (`FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE`): blank/garbage fail open to 1.0 (a workflow typo can never red a leg); clamps to [1.0, 10.0] — the scale never SHRINKS a budget and never turns a real hang into an unbounded wait.
- `FaCliHarness` + `CliVisualHarness` — every wait budget (`waitForBoot/Text/Screen/Raw/Output`, settle, raw-settle grace) multiplied by the ambient scale. Unset → 1.0 → byte-identical legacy behavior locally and in the nightly (nightly stays unsupervised flake evidence for quarantine decisions).
- `ci.yml` — `FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE: '2'` on exactly the two legs the issue names: `PTY/CLI integration (linux, shard N/3)` and `Terminal visual (PTY screenshots, PR)`.
- Regression tests: `test/cli/pty_wait_budget_test.dart` (10 unit tests, no PTY needed — parse semantics, clamping, multiplication, overflow safety).

## Scope discipline

- Sibling lanes (#1385 #1413 #1422 #1467 #1469) keep ownership of their tests' content fixes — this changes zero test files' logic, only the shared wait ceilings the dispatch waves blow through.
- Quarantined files untouched; no `scripts/test_quarantine.json` churn.
- Nightly + integration-mock legs deliberately left unscaled.
- The per-test duration budget gate (#928) is unaffected: green-run durations don't change (match-exits stay early; only give-up deadlines stretch), and the gate never sees red-run durations (`needs: [pty-integration-linux]`).

## Local gates

- `dart analyze` on all changed Dart files: zero issues (full-repo analyze: 132 pre-existing infos identical with/without the diff — analyzer-version skew, none in changed files).
- `dart format`: clean.
- `dart test test/cli/pty_wait_budget_test.dart test/ci_pty_artifact_upload_retry_guard_test.dart`: 14/14 green (incl. the YAML-shape guard over the edited ci.yml).
- flutter_app: `flutter analyze test/cli_visual/cli_visual_harness.dart` clean; `flutter test test/cli_visual/cli_visual_harness_env_test.dart` 14/14 green (verified on a local Flutter 3.47.5 copy).
- Live PTY execution is impossible in this sandbox (`openpty` denied, `/tmp` read-only) — the four drilled CI runs above are the reproduction evidence; the change is exercised by the merge-blocking legs themselves on the next SM validation.

## Remaining

- None in this lane. Un-quarantine decisions for the five sibling tests ride their own issues; if their budgets (not their content) were the binding constraint, this seam already covers them via the same harness paths.

- run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      # gh-1300: the AOT binary built once per run by fa-aot-build. The
      # guard FAILS the shard loudly if the artifact is missing or dead —
      # a silent JIT fallback would hide the optimization from AC1's
      # before/after numbers.
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: fa-aot-bin
          path: fa-local/bundle
      # Artifact zips do NOT preserve the exec bit (download-artifact
      # README: "post-download the file is no longer guaranteed to be set
      # as an executable"). Run 37446280743: `test -x` below failed
      # silently ~20 ms in on EVERY shard — the gate went red before a
      # single test ran. Restore the mode the build job shipped; the
      # smoke below still verifies the restored binary is executable and
      # boots (never a silent JIT fallback). Content integrity is not
      # affected: download-artifact digest-validates (digest-mismatch:
      # error default), so this chmod only ever touches the verified
      # bundle the fa-aot-build job produced.
      - name: Restore exec bit (artifact zips drop permissions)
        run: chmod +x fa-local/bundle/bin/fah
      - name: Smoke the AOT binary (fail loud, never JIT-fallback)
        run: |
          test -x fa-local/bundle/bin/fah
          ./fa-local/bundle/bin/fah --version
      - name: dart test --tags integration (linux, shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/3)
        env:
          # gh-1300 FA_BIN seam: every CLI spawn (pty_harness + the
          # headless helpers via faCliCommand) runs the AOT binary —

          # are all single tests popping quiet-runner budgets inside

    # THE PR PTY/CLI integration leg (gh-1005: the former mac leg merged in;
    # before that, issue #931 part 2 sharded ONE ~40-min job into 3
    # duration-balanced shards — scripts/test_integration_shards.json,
    # file-level units). New integration-tagged files bin-pack in at runtime

    # silently skips it. Explicit --concurrency=4 bounds in-suite
    # parallelism (part 3.3 — package:test forbids `concurrency` in
    # dart_test.yaml tag overrides, so the knob lives here; it bounds
    # concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB — the rate-limit rationale is
    # documented on the llm tag in dart_test.yaml).
    # Per-shard coverage artifacts merge in pty-coverage-gate —
    # a single shard's ratchet would see partial lib/src/cli coverage
    # and false-regress. Each shard also emits the dart json
    # file-reporter: junit feeds rebalancing/budget-tightening PRs, the
    # raw json feeds the #928 duration gate (pty-coverage-gate below).
    # gh-1300: needs the once-per-run AOT build; FA_BIN points every CLI
    # spawn (PTY harness + headless helpers) at the prebuilt binary.
    needs: [fa-aot-build]
    name: PTY/CLI integration (linux, shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/3)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    # 40 > 30: the leg now carries the coverage + file-reporter overhead the
    # old mac leg had (the coverage-free linux twin never paid it) and arm64
    # Graviton cores run somewhat slower than the M-series minis did — margin
    # without stretching the watchdog much.
    timeout-minutes: 40
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1, 2]
    env:
      # Secret shape (review 2026-09-23): this is the pull_request-time leg
      # that receives real provider secrets. GitHub withholds secrets from
      # forks, so external contributions never see them — but every
      # SAME-REPO branch runs this suite with the keys in its process
      # environment before human review (this repo's agent-authored-branch
      # model). The marginal escalation vs the nightly (same suites, same
      # keys, post-merge on main) is small and the watchdog already hands
      # RELEASE_PAT to same-repo PRs; documented here so the assumption is
      # explicit, not implicit.
      #
      # The live-provider legs (unlocked by these keys) load extra
      # lib/src/cli surface into the coverage measurement, so a no-key run
      # measures a DIFFERENT — lower-numbered — value; missing keys (forks)
      # self-skip those legs gracefully and the gate stays honest either
      # way.
      OPENROUTER_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENROUTER_API_KEY }}
      ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
      GOOGLE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GOOGLE_API_KEY }}

## PR Description

Fixes #1391

## Root cause (drilled, not guessed)

All four drillable PTY-family reds in the #1391 window show the SAME signature — one test popping a quiet-runner wait budget inside an otherwise-green 60–70-test shard:

| run / job | failing test | signature |
|---|---|---|
| 114115713413 (PTY shard 0/3) | header_badge_pty (#1469) | `TimeoutException after 30s` waiting the fold badge while a double-compaction turn was still painting |
| 114064133950 (PTY shard 2/3) | fa_tui_follow_pty (#1467) | `expect(contains 'above fold')` read a frame from a LATER state — raced mid-run capture |
| 113385178088 (PTY shard 0/3) | pty_resume_equivalence (#1422) | live transcript captured one probe behind the resumed one — capture raced the turn |
| 114167806111 (PTY shard 0/3) | header_badge_pty (#1469) | same 30s budget pop on a different head |

Mechanism: SM dispatch waves run 2+ full CI runs concurrently on the hosted ubuntu-24.04-arm pool (refresh waves supersede PR heads mid-run); every CLI spawn, mock-LLM round trip, compaction pass and TUI repaint stretches, and fixed wall-clock budgets (harness defaults 10–90s, per-test up to 60s) pop. Window-intermittent, dispatch-correlated — matches the fleet tally in the issue (9 green re-roll heads vs 2 red dispatch windows; canary green).

## Delivered

- `lib/src/cli/pty_wait_budget.dart` — flutter-free, env-injected scale resolver (`FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE`): blank/garbage fail open to 1.0 (a workflow typo can never red a leg); clamps to [1.0, 10.0] — the scale never SHRINKS a budget and never turns a real hang into an unbounded wait.
- `FaCliHarness` + `CliVisualHarness` — every wait budget (`waitForBoot/Text/Screen/Raw/Output`, settle, raw-settle grace) multiplied by the ambient scale. Unset → 1.0 → byte-identical legacy behavior locally and in the nightly (nightly stays unsupervised flake evidence for quarantine decisions).
- `ci.yml` — `FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE: '2'` on exactly the two legs the issue names: `PTY/CLI integration (linux, shard N/3)` and `Terminal visual (PTY screenshots, PR)`.
- Regression tests: `test/cli/pty_wait_budget_test.dart` (10 unit tests, no PTY needed — parse semantics, clamping, multiplication, overflow safety).

## Scope discipline

- Sibling lanes (#1385 #1413 #1422 #1467 #1469) keep ownership of their tests' content fixes — this changes zero test files' logic, only the shared wait ceilings the dispatch waves blow through.
- Quarantined files untouched; no `scripts/test_quarantine.json` churn.
- Nightly + integration-mock legs deliberately left unscaled.
- The per-test duration budget gate (#928) is unaffected: green-run durations don't change (match-exits stay early; only give-up deadlines stretch), and the gate never sees red-run durations (`needs: [pty-integration-linux]`).

## Local gates

- `dart analyze` on all changed Dart files: zero issues (full-repo analyze: 132 pre-existing infos identical with/without the diff — analyzer-version skew, none in changed files).

# pr-1488: fix(1391): load-aware PTY wait budgets — FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE on the two merge-blocking PTY legs

## Description

Fixes #1391

## Root cause (drilled, not guessed)

All four drillable PTY-family reds in the #1391 window show the SAME signature — one test popping a quiet-runner wait budget inside an otherwise-green 60–70-test shard:

| run / job | failing test | signature |
|---|---|---|
| 114115713413 (PTY shard 0/3) | header_badge_pty (#1469) | `TimeoutException after 30s` waiting the fold badge while a double-compaction turn was still painting |
| 114064133950 (PTY shard 2/3) | fa_tui_follow_pty (#1467) | `expect(contains 'above fold')` read a frame from a LATER state — raced mid-run capture |
| 113385178088 (PTY shard 0/3) | pty_resume_equivalence (#1422) | live transcript captured one probe behind the resumed one — capture raced the turn |
| 114167806111 (PTY shard 0/3) | header_badge_pty (#1469) | same 30s budget pop on a different head |

Mechanism: SM dispatch waves run 2+ full CI runs concurrently on the hosted ubuntu-24.04-arm pool (refresh waves supersede PR heads mid-run); every CLI spawn, mock-LLM round trip, compaction pass and TUI repaint stretches, and fixed wall-clock budgets (harness defaults 10–90s, per-test up to 60s) pop. Window-intermittent, dispatch-correlated — matches the fleet tally in the issue (9 green re-roll heads vs 2 red dispatch windows; canary green).

## Delivered

- `lib/src/cli/pty_wait_budget.dart` — flutter-free, env-injected scale resolver (`FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE`): blank/garbage fail open to 1.0 (a workflow typo can never red a leg); clamps to [1.0, 10.0] — the scale never SHRINKS a budget and never turns a real hang into an unbounded wait.
- `FaCliHarness` + `CliVisualHarness` — every wait budget (`waitForBoot/Text/Screen/Raw/Output`, settle, raw-settle grace) multiplied by the ambient scale. Unset → 1.0 → byte-identical legacy behavior locally and in the nightly (nightly stays unsupervised flake evidence for quarantine decisions).
- `ci.yml` — `FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE: '2'` on exactly the two legs the issue names: `PTY/CLI integration (linux, shard N/3)` and `Terminal visual (PTY screenshots, PR)`.
- Regression tests: `test/cli/pty_wait_budget_test.dart` (10 unit tests, no PTY needed — parse semantics, clamping, multiplication, overflow safety).

- Sibling lanes (#1385 #1413 #1422 #1467 #1469) keep ownership of their tests' content fixes — this changes zero test files' logic, only the shared wait ceilings the dispatch waves blow through.

- run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:

          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      # guard FAILS the shard loudly if the artifact is missing or dead —
      # a silent JIT fallback would hide the optimization from AC1's
      # before/after numbers.
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: fa-aot-bin
          path: fa-local/bundle
      # Artifact zips do NOT preserve the exec bit (download-artifact
      # README: "post-download the file is no longer guaranteed to be set
      # as an executable"). Run 37446280743: `test -x` below failed
      # silently ~20 ms in on EVERY shard — the gate went red before a
      # single test ran. Restore the mode the build job shipped; the
      # smoke below still verifies the restored binary is executable and
      # boots (never a silent JIT fallback). Content integrity is not
      # affected: download-artifact digest-validates (digest-mismatch:
      # error default), so this chmod only ever touches the verified
      # bundle the fa-aot-build job produced.
      - name: Restore exec bit (artifact zips drop permissions)
        run: chmod +x fa-local/bundle/bin/fah
      - name: Smoke the AOT binary (fail loud, never JIT-fallback)

          test -x fa-local/bundle/bin/fah

pty-integration-linux:
    # THE PR PTY/CLI integration leg (gh-1005: the former mac leg merged in;
    # before that, issue #931 part 2 sharded ONE ~40-min job into 3
    # duration-balanced shards — scripts/test_integration_shards.json,
    # file-level units). New integration-tagged files bin-pack in at runtime
    # (shard_files.py --tags integration), so a PR adding one never
    # silently skips it. Explicit --concurrency=4 bounds in-suite
    # parallelism (part 3.3 — package:test forbids `concurrency` in
    # dart_test.yaml tag overrides, so the knob lives here; it bounds
    # concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB — the rate-limit rationale is
    # documented on the llm tag in dart_test.yaml).
    # Per-shard coverage artifacts merge in pty-coverage-gate —
    # a single shard's ratchet would see partial lib/src/cli coverage
    # and false-regress. Each shard also emits the dart json
    # file-reporter: junit feeds rebalancing/budget-tightening PRs, the
    # raw json feeds the #928 duration gate (pty-coverage-gate below).
    # gh-1300: needs the once-per-run AOT build; FA_BIN points every CLI
    # spawn (PTY harness + headless helpers) at the prebuilt binary.
    needs: [fa-aot-build]
    name: PTY/CLI integration (linux, shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/3)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    # 40 > 30: the leg now carries the coverage + file-reporter overhead the
    # old mac leg had (the coverage-free linux twin never paid it) and arm64
    # Graviton cores run somewhat slower than the M-series minis did — margin
    # without stretching the watchdog much.
    timeout-minutes: 40
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1, 2]
    env:
      # Secret shape (review 2026-09-23): this is the pull_request-time leg
      # that receives real provider secrets. GitHub withholds secrets from
      # forks, so external contributions never see them — but every
      # SAME-REPO branch runs this suite with the keys in its process
      # environment before human review (this repo's agent-authored-branch
      # model). The marginal escalation vs the nightly (same suites, same
      # keys, post-merge on main) is small and the watchdog already hands
      # RELEASE_PAT to same-repo PRs; documented here so the assumption is
      # explicit, not implicit.
      #
      # The live-provider legs (unlocked by these keys) load extra
      # lib/src/cli surface into the coverage measurement, so a no-key run
      # measures a DIFFERENT — lower-numbered — value; missing keys (forks)
      # self-skip those legs gracefully and the gate stays honest either
      # way.
      OPENROUTER_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENROUTER_API_KEY }}
      ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
      GOOGLE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GOOGLE_API_KEY }}
      OLLAMA_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OLLAMA_API_KEY }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared

- **Title**: fix(1391): load-aware PTY wait budgets — FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE on the two merge-blocking PTY legs
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1391-pty-visual-flake` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 5
- **Additions**: +208

- **Created**: 2026-10-10T12:10:44Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T12:10:44Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1391

## Root cause (drilled, not guessed)

All four drillable PTY-family reds in the #1391 window show the SAME signature — one test popping a quiet-runner wait budget inside an otherwise-green 60–70-test shard:

| run / job | failing test | signature |
|---|---|---|
| 114115713413 (PTY shard 0/3) | header_badge_pty (#1469) | `TimeoutException after 30s` waiting the fold badge while a double-compaction turn was still painting |
| 114064133950 (PTY shard 2/3) | fa_tui_follow_pty (#1467) | `expect(contains 'above fold')` read a frame from a LATER state — raced mid-run capture |
| 113385178088 (PTY shard 0/3) | pty_resume_equivalence (#1422) | live transcript captured one probe behind the resumed one — capture raced the turn |
| 114167806111 (PTY shard 0/3) | header_badge_pty (#1469) | same 30s budget pop on a different head |

Mechanism: SM dispatch waves run 2+ full CI runs concurrently on the hosted ubuntu-24.04-arm pool (refresh waves supersede PR heads mid-run); every CLI spawn, mock-LLM round trip, compaction pass and TUI repaint stretches, and fixed wall-clock budgets (harness defaults 10–90s, per-test up to 60s) pop. Window-intermittent, dispatch-correlated — matches the fleet tally in the issue (9 green re-roll heads vs 2 red dispatch windows; canary green).

## Delivered

- `lib/src/cli/pty_wait_budget.dart` — flutter-free, env-injected scale resolver (`FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE`): blank/garbage fail open to 1.0 (a workflow typo can never red a leg); clamps to [1.0, 10.0] — the scale never SHRINKS a budget and never turns a real hang into an unbounded wait.
- `FaCliHarness` + `CliVisualHarness` — every wait budget (`waitForBoot/Text/Screen/Raw/Output`, settle, raw-settle grace) multiplied by the ambient scale. Unset → 1.0 → byte-identical legacy behavior locally and in the nightly (nightly stays unsupervised flake evidence for quarantine decisions).
- `ci.yml` — `FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE: '2'` on exactly the two legs the issue names: `PTY/CLI integration (linux, shard N/3)` and `Terminal visual (PTY screenshots, PR)`.
- Regression tests: `test/cli/pty_wait_budget_test.dart` (10 unit tests, no PTY needed — parse semantics, clamping, multiplication, overflow safety).

## Scope discipline

- Sibling lanes (#1385 #1413 #1422 #1467 #1469) keep ownership of their tests' content fixes — this changes zero test files' logic, only the shared wait ceilings the dispatch waves blow through.
- Quarantined files untouched; no `scripts/test_quarantine.json` churn.
- Nightly + integration-mock legs deliberately left unscaled.
- The per-test duration budget gate (#928) is unaffected: green-run durations don't change (match-exits stay early; only give-up deadlines stretch), and the gate never sees red-run durations (`needs: [pty-integration-linux]`).

## Local gates

- `dart analyze` on all changed Dart files: zero issues (full-repo analyze: 132 pre-existing infos identical with/without the diff — analyzer-version skew, none in changed files).
- `dart format`: clean.
- `dart test test/cli/pty_wait_budget_test.dart test/ci_pty_artifact_upload_retry_guard_test.dart`: 14/14 green (incl. the YAML-shape guard over the edited ci.yml).
- flutter_app: `flutter analyze test/cli_visual/cli_visual_harness.dart` clean; `flutter test test/cli_visual/cli_visual_harness_env_test.dart` 14/14 green (verified on a local Flutter 3.47.5 copy).
- Live PTY execution is impossible in this sandbox (`openpty` denied, `/tmp` read-only) — the four drilled CI runs above are the reproduction evidence; the change is exercised by the merge-blocking legs themselves on the next SM validation.

## Remaining

- None in this lane. Un-quarantine decisions for the five sibling tests ride their own issues; if their budgets (not their content) were the binding constraint, this seam already covers them via the same harness paths.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1488
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1488
- **Title**: fix(1391): load-aware PTY wait budgets — FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE on the two merge-blocking PTY legs
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1391-pty-visual-flake` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 5
- **Additions**: +208
- **Deletions**: -8
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T12:10:44Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T12:10:44Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1391

## Root cause (drilled, not guessed)

All four drillable PTY-family reds in the #1391 window show the SAME signature — one test popping a quiet-runner wait budget inside an otherwise-green 60–70-test shard:

| run / job | failing test | signature |
|---|---|---|
| 114115713413 (PTY shard 0/3) | header_badge_pty (#1469) | `TimeoutException after 30s` waiting the fold badge while a double-compaction turn was still painting |
| 114064133950 (PTY shard 2/3) | fa_tui_follow_pty (#1467) | `expect(contains 'above fold')` read a frame from a LATER state — raced mid-run capture |
| 113385178088 (PTY shard 0/3) | pty_resume_equivalence (#1422) | live transcript captured one probe behind the resumed one — capture raced the turn |
| 114167806111 (PTY shard 0/3) | header_badge_pty (#1469) | same 30s budget pop on a different head |

Mechanism: SM dispatch waves run 2+ full CI runs concurrently on the hosted ubuntu-24.04-arm pool (refresh waves supersede PR heads mid-run); every CLI spawn, mock-LLM round trip, compaction pass and TUI repaint stretches, and fixed wall-clock budgets (harness defaults 10–90s, per-test up to 60s) pop. Window-intermittent, dispatch-correlated — matches the fleet tally in the issue (9 green re-roll heads vs 2 red dispatch windows; canary green).

## Delivered

- `lib/src/cli/pty_wait_budget.dart` — flutter-free, env-injected scale resolver (`FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE`): blank/garbage fail open to 1.0 (a workflow typo can never red a leg); clamps to [1.0, 10.0] — the scale never SHRINKS a budget and never turns a real hang into an unbounded wait.
- `FaCliHarness` + `CliVisualHarness` — every wait budget (`waitForBoot/Text/Screen/Raw/Output`, settle, raw-settle grace) multiplied by the ambient scale. Unset → 1.0 → byte-identical legacy behavior locally and in the nightly (nightly stays unsupervised flake evidence for quarantine decisions).
- `ci.yml` — `FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE: '2'` on exactly the two legs the issue names: `PTY/CLI integration (linux, shard N/3)` and `Terminal visual (PTY screenshots, PR)`.
- Regression tests: `test/cli/pty_wait_budget_test.dart` (10 unit tests, no PTY needed — parse semantics, clamping, multiplication, overflow safety).

## Scope discipline

- Sibling lanes (#1385 #1413 #1422 #1467 #1469) keep ownership of their tests' content fixes — this changes zero test files' logic, only the shared wait ceilings the dispatch waves blow through.
- Quarantined files untouched; no `scripts/test_quarantine.json` churn.
- Nightly + integration-mock legs deliberately left unscaled.
- The per-test duration budget gate (#928) is unaffected: green-run durations don't change (match-exits stay early; only give-up deadlines stretch), and the gate never sees red-run durations (`needs: [pty-integration-linux]`).

## Local gates

- `dart analyze` on all changed Dart files: zero issues (full-repo analyze: 132 pre-existing infos identical with/without the diff — analyzer-version skew, none in changed files).
- `dart format`: clean.
- `dart test test/cli/pty_wait_budget_test.dart test/ci_pty_artifact_upload_retry_guard_test.dart`: 14/14 green (incl. the YAML-shape guard over the edited ci.yml).
- flutter_app: `flutter analyze test/cli_visual/cli_visual_harness.dart` clean; `flutter test test/cli_visual/cli_visual_harness_env_test.dart` 14/14 green (verified on a local Flutter 3.47.5 copy).
- Live PTY execution is impossible in this sandbox (`openpty` denied, `/tmp` read-only) — the four drilled CI runs above are the reproduction evidence; the change is exercised by the merge-blocking legs themselves on the next SM validation.

## Remaining

- None in this lane. Un-quarantine decisions for the five sibling tests ride their own issues; if their budgets (not their content) were the binding constraint, this seam already covers them via the same harness paths.
